title: What Happens When a Retailer Drops a Product Category? Investigating the Consequences of Ending Tobacco Sales
eligible_reason: Not a staggered design, and the data are simulated. The retailer (EC, i.e., CVS) stopped selling tobacco in September 2014, a single common date. Treated stores are those within 1 km of an EC store, and controls are stores more than 2.5 km away. Columns add a time-varying cigarette price index and treatment x distance/size interactions. The FE set is retailer-state-week, county-week, store-year and store-month-of-year (no plain unit FE). The main demand estimates are IV/LIML.
design_notes: code.R: felm(log.cig.sales ~ dummy [+ dummy:ec_dist + dummy:tot.size ...] + price.idx | ChainStateWeek + CountyWeek + StoreYear + StoreMonthY | 0 | store_id), with dummy = treat x afterSep14. Price regressions on dummy. Reduced-form log non-tobacco sales on dummy. OLS, 2SLS and LIML of log.sales on price.idx and log.cig.sales, instrumented by the treatment and its interactions.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. The ReadMe says the dataset 'is simulated and bears no relationship to the real data used in the paper' (Nielsen RMS). The code is illustrative only.
